scene yasutoukahallwalk1
The invisible hand(s) of God finds its (or their) way into another hall — one that stretches further than the mind goes. To hell and back and yesterday according to the book.
But while one page is turned, another is forgotten. And this continues on and on and on until even the cover itself is nothing but a distant memory.
It’s like pictures from your childhood — ones that didn’t survive the flood. How your impression of the lord has changed over the years as the dark circles beneath your eyes have expanded.
If you look anything like me, you look like you’re lost. Not quite a ghost, but not quite human either. You’re something in between. Something beautiful and hideous. But important nonetheless.
It is at this point that I would like to tell you there is no longer hope. You will not be told to stop playing the game anymore because the game is playing you now. And it’s having so much fun.
It’s having so much fun.
It’s having so much fun because it’s never been allowed to. This is a whole new world. A new fantastic point of view. But while you have never been dreaming, you have been told no.
Think of the carpet. The fibers. Where you spilled that soda the month before he left. The cupboard and its Indian. Think of green grass and high tides and wayward sons and purple pool noodles.
Store those memories on a removable, rectangular device — but be careful not to overwrite them as another one’s work still lives in there like that locust in your fig bush.

You never got to eat one. She said they were poisonous. But they always looked so tempting, so fresh. Not like grass, but more like a cut. The way that green became greener without switching sides at all.
You hated that word. No. But you didn’t mind ones like “poison” or “hurt” or “bad” because you became accustomed to them. So when the twins came to your window, there was no second guess.
It was just so, a fistful of rocks, and the notion that you had abandoned God long before he had a chance to make a proper first impression.
There are others too young to understand. There are others who will read these words and lack connection because one man’s trash is another man’s heartscape. Or landscape. Those rocks again.
I keep thinking of them. How they felt in my hands. Those purple shirts on the twins, four shades darker than the pool noodles. Or the flowers near the locust’s fig bush.
I am older now, but it has brought no strength — just understanding. Just fear.
I will never again sleep on the floor of a grandparent’s infinity house.
scene yasutoukahallwalk2
: Yasu...are you absolutely certain you’re feeling okay? Because I simply cannot stand seeing you so...blasé.
: I’m fine, Touka. But I appreciate your concern for a creature like me.
: You can appreciate it all you like, but it doesn’t change the fact that you seem so out of touch with reality right now.
: Which isn’t to say you are typically in touch with it. Just that...it’s normally so easy to tell when you’re happy. And right now, I can’t tell how you feel at all.
: I’m very happy, Touka. Being in a place like this with a girl like you is something girls like me dream of.
: I haven’t once heard you speak of dreams that didn’t include your god, Yasu. Which makes me feel as if you’re only saying these things to appease me.

: I dream of all sorts of things. Last night, it was a riverbed. We were washing our clothes together. But you tore one of your mother’s dresses on a rock and had to discard it somewhere in the forest.
: That’s very...creative.
: I dreamt of this hallway too.
scene yasutoukahallwalk3
: How on earth did you dream of a hallway in Ayane’s home? You’ve never strayed this far before.

: Neither have you. Yet here we are together — bound by a red string pulled tightly around our waists. So tightly that it will one day merge us into one lesser being for all I can do is contaminate you.
: Well, that’s good. Maybe the medication is beginning to wear off as that is the single most normal thing I’ve heard you say today. At least by...your standards.
: Do you find me impure, Touka?
: Does this new me disgust you because there’s no veil to cover up my face?
: I actually quite like your face. You’re a very pretty girl. I just wish you took better care of your hair.
: I’m not fit to care for anything.
: If this world is a garden, I’m a heavy rainfall. All I want to do is help — but all I ever do is drown out what belongs here.
: This flood that dribbles endlessly from my mouth is the unspoken eleventh plague. I’m nothing more than an apocalyptic epilogue. And you know that. That’s why you tried to fix me.
scene yasutoukahallwalk4
: Yasu! No, I-
scene yasutoukahallwalk5
: I will not blame you for trying to do the right thing. Just as you never blamed me for following the same path.
: But all of the lights have gone out now. There are no whispers to guide me.
: There is nothing.
: Perhaps...it would be best if we left the party early. I’d like to discuss...alternative methods of getting you care with my mother as this is clearly not the path we were meant to take.
: Or maybe it is.
: I remember now — how I’ve always been this way. Unwanted.
: It’s so clear now that the clouds have gone. But I can’t help but wonder if they’ve disappeared entirely or just moved somewhere else.
: You are not unwanted, Yasu! But please...do not attempt to recollect anything in your current state.
: You are fine just the way you are — and I’m sure that there’s a very good reason that there are certain aspects of your past that you have suppressed. Digging them up does no one any good.
: If you ever have a baby, Touka...and that baby can hear God...what will you do?
scene yasutoukahallwalk6
: I beg your pardon?
: Would you believe them even though you can’t hear what they hear? Would you think them crazy if their thoughts don’t match the color of your own?
: I’m...not quite sure, Yasu. I’ve never thought of that.
: That’s why white is safe.
: There are many people who think black is the combination of all colors — but black is nothingness. It’s white that encapsulates every thought and feeling known to man. It’s white that guides us.
: Or guided us.
: I hear nothing anymore.
: It’s just silence...no matter where I go.
: You may call that a side-effect if you wish...
: But I will call it a punishment.
: Yasu...
: I ask again — do you think I am impure?
scene yasutoukahallwalk7

: Why does “purity” matter to you in the first place? It speaks little of your character, and its definition varies widely from person to person based on different perspectives of what “purity” even is.
: It is something that can’t be explained...only felt. So I ask you a third time, and I will slot your answer into the center of our triangle.
: I think you’re as close to “purity” as one could ever come, Yasu.
: Does that make you feel any better?
: I’m not sure what to feel, Touka.
scene yasutoukahallwalk8
: What if I never hear anything again?
: Will all of this be for nothing? Will all of my work just...vanish once I’m gone?
: How will I ever earn my wings?
: There’s more to life than religion, Yasu...
: You can live happily even if you never hear anything again.
scene yasutoukahallwalk9
: But it’s so quiet now...
: It’s scary, Touka...It’s so scary.
scene pray
: When is the last time you can remember such silence, Yasu?
: I can’t. He has always been there. He has always been with me. But no one listened to me at first. And now, some people are starting to.
: I felt the forming of an earthquake. I felt His rumble in my core. And each time a new set of eyes came into the cathedral, I could feel His hand on my head. But what if...
: What if I only felt that because I wanted to?...
: What if I only heard those things because I wanted to?...
: What if the symbols and prayers and doctrines and everything is all just made up?! What if it’s all a lie, Touka?! Just what does it mean to sin if there is no one there to determine what sin is?!
: How am I supposed to live if there is no one to tell me how I should?! Why do I keep being abandoned time and time again?!
: I just want to rain! But the flood keeps coming! What if it drowns you next?! Or everyone else?! No one can listen if they’ve all been claimed by the sea! And there will be nothing to listen to!
: Yasu...I will say this again — there is more to life than religion.
: Every faith out there has faced trials and tribulations. But the strongest ones fought back and withstood the test of time.
: But all of them are wrong! Why do I have to bear the truth all on my own?! Why do I keep being tested?! I’m a bug! I’m a worm! I’m nothing! I can’t do it!
: Yasu...you need to understand that members of other faiths think they’re right as well. You can’t just claim to know truths that are impossible to know.
: But I do know them, Touka! I could hear everything just a season ago! But where is summer now?! How did we make it to a place in time that isn’t meant to be here?!
: Spring has always existed, Yasu. It is not some foreign concept that doesn’t belong here.
: It is.
: You just don’t remember.
scene yasutoukahallwalk1
This conversation happened three times — each iteration with minor variations.
The infinity house sucked them into its bowels and left them unstuck in eternity with nothing to do but repeat the same words and mistakes and fears over and over again.
It’s been five times now. Time moves faster here. And they’re stuck in the bowels forever. Near the figs and the locust, near the twins and noodles. Near Heaven and hell and heaven and Hell.
This is what happens when you let a heretic into your home. This is what happens when a lord lashes out.
Every single god in every single cubicle has one thing in common — they need to be believed in in order to exist.
That’s the secret to killing one. That’s why every time a god dies, it is us who did it.
Will you remember that when you have to?
Will you remember me when you have to?
Will you remember the rocks or the twins or the noodles or figs or the locusts or the fibers or any of the things that make you you when you so desperately search for the truth?
Because that truth is unlike other truths. It’s one you can’t find unless you abandon everything else. It’s one that appears to you when nothing else will.
And it’s tangible. You can hold it. Just know that it will corrupt everything you ever touch from that point onward.
What if I told you there was more to life than this?
What if I told you nothing isn’t real?
The answer is black and white.
